decisionsTitle: «Schimbă adresa»: an Administrator moves a registration to another address (reversing «no verified-email edit» and §645's locked address)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-11-11:** «aparent nu pot modifica mailul unei persoane???». Told that the address cannot be changed by the team, on purpose — the address is the person's identity, their links and their declaration go to it, and the written rule says «the address stays the person's» — and offered three answers (only the addresses the person never confirmed, the recommended one; leave the rule as it is; any address, at any time, not recommended), he chose **«Orice adresă, oricând»**: the Administrator may change any address, a confirmed one included.

**Decision — this REVERSES «no verified-email edit» (`DECISIONS.md` §33, §67, BR-REQ-037-03 criterion 2) and «Modifică datele»'s locked address (§645), on the owner's instruction.** A new Administrator-only verb, «Schimbă adresa», on the registration's own card «Adresa de email» (beside «Datele înscrierii», never inside it): one registration per press, in any state, at any time.

1. **The data move.** `participants.canonical_email` stays the immutable identity (`AGENTS.md` §10.4): no participant row is ever rewritten or merged. The registration is re-pointed — `registrations.participant_id` set to the participant of the new canonical address, reused exactly as it is (its name and language untouched; `findOrCreateParticipant`, which refreshes both on an unverified row, is not used) or created, unverified, with the registration's name and language. Under the event's lock, in one transaction, the row read again under it (`service.ts#changeRegistrationAddressByStaff`). The state, the place, the waiting position and the race number do not move; the allocator is asked nothing. Two nullable columns record it, `address_changed_at` and `address_changed_by_staff_user_id` (migration `0198`); the vouching columns stay the old address's facts.
2. **The links.** Every live action link of the registration is revoked for cause (`invalidated_at`, no `superseded_by_token_id`), so an old link gets the one generic refusal and never «a newer email exists». And every registration-scoped token is **bound** to the registration's current participant, at read and at spend (`action-tokens/repository.ts`): a link whose participant is not the registration's is a missing token — whatever else is true of it (superseded, spent, expired), so the old address learns nothing of where the registration stands. The same holds of the old address's spent invitation link (`/registrations/invitation/[token]?done=1`), whose token names an invitation, not a registration: it speaks of the registration it created only while that registration is still on the invitation's own participant, the one the acceptance used (`token-actions.ts#acceptedRegistrationOfSpentInvitation`); after a move it is answered as a spent link with no registration to speak of — no deadline, no state.
3. **The mail.** The old address's participant messages for the row still waiting and never tried are withdrawn with their club copies, and the renderer withdraws a retry or a claimed one (`render.ts`, `OutboxMessageWithdrawn`): no link is ever minted for the old address. The event's own news still waiting — a reminder, the organizers' message, a change or cancellation of the event, the thanks (`service.ts#FOLLOWS_THE_MOVE`) — carries no link of the old address and is re-addressed to the new participant instead, so a message queued before the move is not lost: every such row still `PENDING`, whatever its attempts, a retry waiting between two attempts included, so its next attempt renders for the registration's current participant; only a row a worker has claimed at that moment (`PROCESSING`) stays the old address's, and the renderer withdraws it. A notice to an address the registration was moved back to since is withdrawn at render: nothing true is left to tell it. The club's archive and notice keep their own rules.
4. **What each address is told.** Two new message types, neither carrying a token (migration `0197`, an `ADD VALUE` of its own): `REGISTRATION_ADDRESS_REMOVED` to the old address — the organizers changed the address of «name»'s registration at the event, its links no longer work, and the contact page if this was not asked for; never the new address; queued whatever that address's refusals say — and `REGISTRATION_ADDRESS_ADDED` to the new address — it now receives the registration's emails, where the registration stands, whether the next step follows, the contact page if it is not theirs. The question before the press («Schimbi adresa?») says which of the two the move will do — the next step to the new address, or only the two notices with no step for the new address to take; always, that the event's emails not sent yet go to the new address (the news that follows the move, point 3, which may still be waiting after a cancelled or completed event: a cancellation, a thanks), so it never promises the new address no other email; and, while the event is not over, that the old address may get its family's own message again (point 6 of the move: another person on the old address at the event with a step still to take); it never promises the old address silence, chosen on the server by `domain/address-change.ts#moveSendsNextStep`, the move's own rule (`stateMessageOnMove` over `eventOverForMove`), never a second copy of it. The body is the part the club may reword; the dead links, the status and the contact page are the platform's lines after it. Then the state's own message to the new address: the verification with the club's email-link window again from the move, the waiting-list message, the offer, the declaration, or the confirmation with a **new check-in code**, so the QR the old address holds opens nothing. **The confirmation's signed declaration, sent to an address the Administrator typed, carries the identity document masked** — the club's archive copy (`domain/address-change.ts#declarationPdfAudienceAfterMove`) — until the person confirms the new address with its own link after the move: one typo must not send a person's identity document, with the signature's IP and browser beside it, to a stranger's inbox, as a group run's copy is masked for the same reason; the whole copy stays in the backoffice for its seven days.
5. **The trail.** One audit row, `registration.address_changed_by_staff`, on the old participant, the registration as its entity, with ids, counts and flags only — never an address; `familyResentFor` only when the family's message was in fact queued (one condition for both: a family to tell, its message, and the event not over) — scrubbed of the two participant ids by the erase and the retention sweep. A declaration signed afterwards from an emailed link is shown on the registration's page as «semnată din linkul trimis la adresa schimbată de echipă» (`domain/address-change.ts#signedAfterStaffAddressChange`), and a timeline line says when and by whom the address was changed.
6. **The person's record.** «Toate datele unei persoane» shows each address only its own mail: the new address sees the registration and its trail, never the mail sent to the old one; the old address sees its own messages, the notice and the move's row by its participant. Erasing either address acts on its own rows.

**Safeguards that keep every other rule true.** No participant merge and no rewritten participant row (§10.4). Nothing vouched and nothing signed in the same press: the vouching columns (`email_confirmed_at`, `email_confirmed_by_staff_user_id`) stay the old address's facts, and a new participant is created unverified. A row already past its address step (a held place, an offer, a confirmed row) is therefore served at an address neither the person nor staff confirmed — the person's own link from there signs, but does not confirm the address; only a verification link does. The declaration is still the person's, so «no staff-signed declaration» stays checkable — the trail shows the signature as given after a staff address change, never as staff's. The allocator is not touched (no place moves, nobody passes anybody). The old links die twice over — revoked, and refused by the binding. The old address is always told, with no token and without the new address. «Oferte și beneficii» is a consent: withdrawn. Refused, writing nothing, each said at the box: an address that is not one (`ADDRESS_INVALID`); the same address, a provider's variant included (its canonical form or its inbox, `ADDRESS_UNCHANGED`: «the same inbox»); the same runner already on the new address at the event, active or not, or at another event of the race while this one is active — another person's row there too, the race's index being per address (`ADDRESS_ALREADY_HELD`); the new address holding as many rows at the event as the club's rules allow one address — the club's limit, or one while family registration is off (`ADDRESS_HOLDS_ENOUGH`); a family form waiting on the row (`ADDRESS_FAMILY_FORM_PENDING`); an open invitation of the new address to the event, which the moved row would adopt (`ADDRESS_INVITED`); an erased registration (`NOT_FOUND`); a registration erased before the move's read under the event's lock, and — should anything take it after, which the row lock below keeps an erase or retention's sweep from doing — an UPDATE that matches no row (`NOT_FOUND`, never a retry: the whole transaction rolled back, the participant it would have created, the revoked links, the outbox and audit writes with it, so no orphan is left); and a lock cycle or a serialization failure PostgreSQL broke inside the move (40P01, 40001), caught outside the transaction and answered «Nu s-a schimbat nimic: înscrierea se schimba chiar în acel moment. Apasă din nou «Schimbă adresa».» (`ADDRESS_TRY_AGAIN`), nothing written, never raw. A unique violation the checks did not foresee is answered as `ALREADY_ON_ADDRESS` only when the violated constraint, read by its name from the error, is one of the two address indexes (`registrations_event_participant_name_unique`, `registrations_race_participant_active_unique`), never raw; a fresh check-in code that meets another row's (`registrations_checkin_code_unique`) is no refusal — another is drawn, up to five times, each attempt in its own savepoint so the transaction stays usable, and the fifth collision is rethrown as it is — every path of the loop is bounded, so a move always ends and never holds the event's lock in a spin; any other unique violation is rethrown as it is, never told to the Administrator as the address. The Administrator's alone (`canManageRegistrations`), asserted by the action, the wrapper and the service; the Organizer reads the address and gets no form. The family left on the old address with a step still to take is sent the family's own message again, to the old address. The orphan sweep keeps an old participant while its notice of the move is still to leave. Under real concurrency (`tests/concurrency/address-change.test.ts`): two moves onto one address at a limit of one, exactly one succeeds; a move racing a public form of the same runner, one wins and nothing raw reaches the screen — the lock every entry takes before it reads an address serializes them; an erase racing the move of a row that holds no place, both calls end and the row is gone — 20 runs in a row of five rounds each, every round moved and then erased; a link minted (`issueActionToken`) racing the move of a row that consents to offers, both calls end — 20 runs in a row of ten rounds each, every round moved and minted — and the one dangerous interleaving forced on two connections (the minter's token superseded, the move left waiting on it, then the minter's KEY SHARE on the row) is granted at once and the move ends moved, where the earlier order (the consent's withdrawal first) ended in PostgreSQL's 40P01.

**The lock order.** Under the event's lock the move locks the registration row `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` before its links and its mail, and until it holds the links it only reads (and may insert the new address's participant, a row that references no registration). Then, statement for statement: the live tokens revoked; the row `FOR UPDATE` in `setPromoConsent`, when the consent to offers is on — the withdrawal and its audit row unchanged, only moved after the tokens; the waiting outbox rows; and the row `FOR UPDATE` again at its UPDATE, on **every** move, not only a confirmed one's new check-in code: `participant_id` is a key column of the name's unique index (`registrations_event_participant_name_unique`), so PostgreSQL takes `FOR UPDATE` for any UPDATE that sets it. Both `FOR UPDATE`s come after the tokens are held, so neither meets a link being minted in a cycle; the notices' INSERTs take only a KEY SHARE. The paths that write a registration's tokens or outbox rows without the event's lock were listed, with their order, in the function's docstring: the erase of a row holding no place and retention's deletes take the registration row first and its tokens and mail after (the cascade); the drain claims outbox rows alone, and a link minted at its render (`issueActionToken`) holds the registration's live tokens and then takes a KEY SHARE lock on the registration row through its foreign key — tokens first; the mail webhook touches outbox rows alone; the desk's presses take the event's lock or write the registration row alone; a link's own press takes its token and then the event's lock. With both orders present, no `FOR UPDATE` may come before the tokens: it blocks the KEY SHARE of a link being minted while that link's transaction holds the tokens the move goes for next. The first round's order did exactly that whenever the consent to offers was on (the withdrawal ran first and locked the row `FOR UPDATE`); it now runs after the tokens. `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` does not block a KEY SHARE and does block the erase's and retention's DELETE, which now wait for the move — read without a row lock, the two-connection case had the erase aborted by PostgreSQL's deadlock detection (a raw error, the row left) in one run of five. The cycle that remains (a link's press holding its token while it waits for the event's lock the move holds) is answered by the try-again refusal above; a link being minted is not its victim.

**Decided for the owner (the three questions the design left open):**
1. **A hold's or an offer's deadline** is kept; when less than 24 hours remain it becomes 24 hours from the change, capped by the event's start — but for a counted place **never while anybody is eligible on the waiting list**: lengthening a counted hold then would keep a place ahead of the person waiting beyond what the allocator's own deadline gives them (`AGENTS.md` §10.5–§10.6), so the deadline is kept as it was. A place «Pe lista de invitați speciali» takes no counted place and may be lengthened. A deadline already passed, or none, is left to the allocator's own rules.
2. **A cancelled or lapsed registration, or one after the event has ended** (cancelled, completed, or past its end — without one, the next midnight of its start day in its own zone, as every other read of «ended» takes it (`email-state.ts#eventEndSql`), so race day after the start is not over), may be moved: rectification still matters. It gets the two notices alone — no link, no step.
3. **«Vreau să primesc oferte și beneficii»** is withdrawn by the move, audited exactly as staff's withdrawal is (`registration.promo_consent_changed`, `via: STAFF`, on the old address's trail): the consent was given from the old address, and the question before the press says so when the person had given it.

**For the lawyer.** No legal text or template is changed — and the move makes two of the declaration's sentences not always true, for the club and its lawyer to decide whether to reword. After a move, the declaration may be **signed from, and its copy sent to, an address the club typed that neither the person nor staff confirmed**: «Dacă semnez electronic, din linkul trimis pe adresa de email confirmată, …» and «În ambele cazuri primesc o copie pe adresa de email confirmată», both in the paragraph «Semnez personal» (`legal-documents/templates/declaration.ts`). The platform narrows the second: the copy sent there masks the identity document until the person confirms the new address by its own link. The page shows such a signature as «semnată din linkul trimis la adresa schimbată de echipă», and the trail says who changed the address and when. A wording that would stay true is «din linkul trimis pe adresa de email a înscrierii» — the club's to choose at its next revision; until then the club may prefer to move a registration already past its address step only on a request it can trace to the person. Whether the club's texts should say that the organizers may correct a wrong address on request (the privacy notice's «Rectificare: corectăm datele greșite» already covers it) is the club's to word at its next revision.

**Refused inside the verb.** Changing the address and vouching or signing in one press («Dă-i un loc acum» stays a press of its own); a silent change (the two notices are not optional); changing an erased registration; the new address in the old notice or in the trail; merging participant rows, or rewriting `participants.delivery_email`, which every registration on that address shares; moving a whole family in one press (one registration per press); leaving the old links alive (both the revoke and the binding are required); offering the verb to the Organizer or at the desk.
changelogLine: - **«Schimbă adresa»** — an Administrator can now change a registration's email address, on its own card «Adresa de email»: the registration moves to the new address with its place, state and number, every link sent to the old address stops working, both addresses get an email about the change, the new one gets the next step while there is one (a confirmed runner a new QR code) — the question before the press says which — and the consent to offers and benefits is withdrawn. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends the status line and criterion 2. Given the backoffice, when it renders, then it offers no participant merge and rewrites no participant row; an address is changed only by «Schimbă adresa», which re-points one registration to the participant of the new canonical address (2026-11-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 19. Given a registration's page, then the Administrator — and nobody else — is offered «Schimbă adresa» on the card «Adresa de email», the Organizer reading the address with no form; the question before the press says the next step is sent to the new address only when the move sends one (`moveSendsNextStep`, the move's own rule), and otherwise that both addresses are told and the new address gets no step to take — never that it gets no other email — and, always, that the event's emails not sent yet go to the new address, and, while the event is not over, that the old address may get its family's own message again, never promising the old address silence, in both languages; and the words on the rejected-email line and in «Ce îi spui» say to ask for the right address, which an administrator changes in «Adresa de email», never that only the person can, by registering again (2026-11-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given an Administrator moving a registration in any of its seven states to another address, when it commits, then under the event lock and in one transaction `participant_id` is the new canonical address's participant — reused unchanged or created, no participant row rewritten or merged — with `address_changed_at` and `address_changed_by_staff_user_id`; the state, the place, the waiting position and the race number are unchanged; every live link of the registration is revoked for cause; the old address's queued participant mail for it is withdrawn; `REGISTRATION_ADDRESS_REMOVED` (no token, no new address, the contact page) is queued to the old address despite any open refusal, `REGISTRATION_ADDRESS_ADDED` to the new one, then the state's own message — the verification with a fresh window, the waiting list, the offer, the declaration, or the confirmation with a new check-in code — none for a cancelled or lapsed row or an event that is over (with no end of its own, after the next midnight of its start day in its zone); the event's own news still waiting and not claimed (a reminder, the organizers' message, a change, a cancellation, the thanks), whatever its attempts, is re-addressed to the new participant rather than withdrawn and renders for the new address, a claimed one being withdrawn at render; the confirmation's signed declaration to the new address masks the identity document until that address is confirmed by its own link after the move; a hold or offer under a day from its end gets a day from the move, capped by the start, only while nobody waits; «oferte și beneficii» is withdrawn and audited; the old address's family with a step to take is sent its message again; one audit row holds ids and counts and no address, scrubbed by the erase, naming a family resend only when one was queued — none after the event is over; a declaration signed afterwards from an emailed link is shown as signed after a staff address change (2026-11-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given «Schimbă adresa», when the address is not valid, is the same address or a provider's variant of it, already holds this runner at the event (active or not) or at another event of the race, is at the club's limit per address, or has an open invitation to the event, or a family form waits on the row, or the row was erased — before the move's read under the event's lock, or after it, an UPDATE matching no row being `NOT_FOUND`, never retried — or PostgreSQL broke a lock cycle or a serialization inside the move (40P01, 40001), answered «press again» (`ADDRESS_TRY_AGAIN`) — then it is refused with its own sentence at the box and nothing is written, and two moves or a move and a public form racing for one address never reach the database's unique index as a raw failure; an erase racing the move of a row that holds no place waits for the move's row lock, both calls end, the move ending moved, `NOT_FOUND` or «press again», never raw, and the row is gone; a link minted for the registration racing the move of a row that consents to offers meets no lock cycle — the move takes no `FOR UPDATE` on the row before it holds the row's live tokens — both calls end, the link minted and the move moved or «press again»; only the two address indexes are answered as `ALREADY_ON_ADDRESS`, a new check-in code that meets another row's is drawn again and the row moves, and one that meets another row's on all five draws ends the move with an error that is not about the address, nothing written — the move always ends, every loop in it bounded, and any other unique violation is rethrown, never answered as the address (2026-11-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a registration-scoped action token whose participant is not the registration's current one, when it is read or spent for any purpose, then it is answered exactly as a missing token, and a spent invitation link speaks of the registration it created only while that registration is on the invitation's own participant, a moved one answered with no deadline and no state — never «a newer email exists», «already used» or «expired» — and the renderer withdraws a participant message queued for a registration whose participant changed since, the old address's notice of the move excepted unless the registration was moved back to that address since (2026-11-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given «Schimbă adresa», when each of the seven roles presses it, then only the Administrator and the Superadministrator move the registration; every other role is refused FORBIDDEN by the action and, with its gate standing aside, by the service, and nothing is written (2026-11-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a registration moved to another address, when «Toate datele unei persoane» is read for either address, then the new address shows the registration and none of the mail sent to the old one, and the old address shows its own messages, the notice of the move and the move's audit row, never the new address's mail; and the orphan sweep keeps the old participant while its notice of the move is still to leave (2026-11-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: «Schimbă adresa»: an Administrator moves a registration to another address, old links dead, both addresses told
